title: ISOMITTED returns TRUE for any omitted LAMBDA argument (even without [brackets]), and does not lift over arrays
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527, ISOMITTED(argument) returns TRUE only when argument is an omitted LAMBDA parameter—including a non-bracketed parameter whose call passed an empty trailing slot such as =LAMBDA(xx,yy,IF(ISOMITTED(yy),xx,yy))(3,)—and returns FALSE for a supplied value, blank cell, range reference (=ISOMITTED(Data!A1:A3) -> FALSE), or array (=ISOMITTED({2;3}) -> FALSE, without lifting).
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 across fn2_questions (fn2_q015, fn2_q116, fn2_q117), jnt_evaluator_callables (rows 50-53), prefix_metadata (row 245), and recorded array-lift case unswept-00303-isomitted-arg0_array_lift (l1.rs line 488).
